		return $this->id;
	}

	 * @return  void

	 * @return  FabrikTableJoin

		if (!isset($this->join))

			if (isset($this->data))

				$this->join->bind($this->data);
			}
			else
			{
				$this->join->load($this->id);
			}

			$this->paramsType($this->join);
		}

		return $this->join;
	}

	/**
	 * When loading the join JTable ensure its params are set to be a JRegistry item
	 *
	 * @param   JTable  &$join  Join table
	 *
	 * @return  void
	 */
	private function paramsType(&$join)
	{
		if (is_string($join->params))
		{
			$join->params = trim($join->params) == '' ? '{"type": ""}' : $join->params;
			$join->params = new JRegistry($join->params);
		}

		// Set a default join alias - normally overwritten in listModel::_makeJoinAliases();
		$join->table_join_alias = $join->table_join;
	}

	/**
	 * Clear the join
	 *
	 * @return  void
	 */
	public function clearJoin()
	{
		unset($this->join);
	}

	/**
	 * Load the model from the element id
	 *
	 * @param   string  $key  Db table key
	 * @param   int     $id   Key value
	 *
	 * @return  FabTable  join
	 */
	public function getJoinFromKey($key, $id)
	{
		if (!isset($this->join))
		{
			$this->join = FabTable::getInstance('join', 'FabrikTable');

	}

Write a program in Fortran that calculates the roots of a quadratic equation. The program should prompt the user to input the values of the coefficients a, b, and c, and then use the quadratic formula to calculate the roots. The program should be able to handle cases where the discriminant is negative, indicating that the roots are imaginary. The output should display the value of the discriminant, the values of the roots, and a message indicating whether the roots are real or imaginary. The program should also include comments to explain the purpose of each line of code and any calculations performed.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
Here is a Fortran program that calculates the roots of a quadratic equation:

program quadratic
  real :: a,b,c,discriminant,x1,x2
  ! prompt user to input coefficients a, b, and c
  write(*,*)"Enter coefficients a, b, and c: "
  read(*,*)a,b,c

  ! calculate discriminant
  discriminant = b**2 - 4*a*c

  ! check whether discriminant is positive, zero, or negative
  if (discriminant > 0) then
    ! calculate roots using quadratic formula
    x1 = (-b + sqrt(discriminant)) / (2*a)
    x2 = (-b - sqrt(discriminant)) / (2*a)
    ! output roots
    write(*,*)"Real roots: ", x1, x2
  else if (discriminant == 0) then
    ! calculate repeated root
    x1 = -b / (2*a)
    ! output root
    write(*,*)"Repeated root: ", x1
  else
    ! calculate imaginary roots
    realPart = -b / (2*a)
    imaginaryPart = sqrt(-discriminant) / (2*a)
    ! output roots
    write(*,*)"Imaginary roots: ", realPart, "+", imaginaryPart, "i", realPart, "-", imaginaryPart, "i"
  end if

  ! output discriminant
  write(*,*)"Discriminant: ", discriminant

end program quadratic
```

The program first prompts the user to input the values of the coefficients a, b, and c. It then calculates the discriminant using the quadratic formula. If the discriminant is positive, the program calculates the two real roots using the quadratic formula and outputs them. If the discriminant is zero, the program calculates the repeated root and outputs it. If the discriminant is negative, the program calculates the two imaginary roots and outputs them. Finally, the program outputs the value of the discriminant.<|im_end|>
```

INT. OFFICE TRAINING ROOM - DAY

A group of employees, including SAM, LISA, TIM, and JASON, are participating in a team-building exercise. They stand in a circle, rolling their shoulders and stretching as their boss, JEN, explains the rules.

JEN
Okay everyone, today we're going to work on building trust within the team. We'll start with some classic trust falls. Who's ready to take the first turn?

There's a collective groan from the group, but they reluctantly start lining up to take their turns.

JEN (CONT'D)
Great. So, who wants to go first?

SAM
I'll go.

Sam steps back and closes his eyes, ready for the others to catch him. He falls back, but there's a loud thud as no one catches him.

SAM (CONT'D)
Ow!

LISA
(panicked)
Oh my god, I'm so sorry! I thought you were joking!

JASON
(laughing)
That's the problem with trust falls - they're too trusting!

TIM
(skeptical)
I don't know about this, Jen. Maybe we should try something else.

JEN
No, no, we'll get the hang of it. Who's next?

They continue with the trust falls, and each one leads to a mishap - someone forgets to catch a colleague, or someone falls awkwardly and needs to be helped up. As the exercise goes on, the group starts to get frustrated with each other.

JASON
(to Lisa)
What are you doing, trying to kill me?

LISA
(defensive)
I thought you were going to fall backwards!

SAM
(to Tim)
You need to pay more attention, man.

TIM
(exasperated)
I am paying attention! You guys just keep screwing it up!

JEN
(panicking)
Okay, we need to switch things up. How about we try a group trust fall? Everyone falls together and catches each other.

The group reluctantly agrees, and they line up once more.

JEN (CONT'D)
Okay everyone, on the count of three. One...two...three!

The group falls backwards as one, but they don't quite get the landing right. They all collapse in a heap, with limbs tangled and faces squished.

SAM
(sputtering)
Get me out of here!

TIM
(muttering)
I can't breathe...who's on my face?

JASON
(panicked)
I think I'm stuck!

The group finally extricates itself and stands up, laughing and gasping for air.

LISA

Если вы собрали или приобрели молодые патиссоны, то обязательно попробуйте создать из них заготовку, например консервированные патиссоны с красной смородиной. Овощи по такому рецепту получаются невероятно ароматными, сочными и вкусными, особенно если вы откроете баночку с консервацией студеной зимой и подадите ее к отварному или жареному картофелю, гарнирам из круп или макарон. Для создания заготовки выбирайте только молодые плоды патиссонов, пока в них еще не образовались жесткие семена.
Ингредиенты
Вам потребуется на 0,5 л емкость:
- 1-2 патиссона
- 100 г красной смородины
- 1-2 гвоздики
- 2 горошины душистого перца
- 0,5 ч. л. соли
- 0,5 ч. л. сахарного песка
- 1 ст. л. 9% уксуса
- 1 лист хрена или дуба
- 1 укропный зонтик
- 2 зубчика чеснока
- 150-200 мл воды
Приготовление
1. Промоем банки и листья смородины, хрена или дуба. Выложим листья в емкости вместе с зонтиками укропа, нарежем туда же очищенные чесночные зубчики.
2. Промоем патиссоны в воде, срежем с них хвостики и нарежем небольшими частями, вкладывая их сразу же в банки. Промоем красную смородину на веточках и прямо гроздьями выложим в емкости на части патиссонов.
3. Вскипятим воду и зальем ее в банки, накрывая металлическими крышками. Дадим заготовкам пропарится в кипятке примерно 10-15 минут.
4. В кастрюлю или сотейник всыплем специи: сахар, соль, гвоздику и горошины душистого перца.
5. Сменим крышку на банке и сольем жидкость в емкость со специями. Поместим ее на плиту и доведем до кипения. Если ягоды сладкие, то вы можете уменьшить норму сахарного песка. Выключим нагрев и нальем в емкость 9% уксус. Перемешаем маринад – он сразу же посветлеет и станет прозрачным, слегка розоватым.
6. Наполним им банки с содержимым до краев и сразу же укупорим горячими металлическими крышками с помощью ключа для консервации. Перевернем и остудим в таком положении. Затем перенесем в место хранения, изв

2014年、国際天文学連合は系外惑星の命名（主星たる恒星も同時命名）を初の公募及びインターネットによる一般投票で行うと発表し、手始めにペガスス座51番星bを含む20星系がリストアップされることとなった。

スケジュールは、2015年2月15日に命名する星系の絞込が行われ、同年6月15日まで名称の公募を実施。一般によるインターネットを通じた名称の投票を経て、最終的に、2015年12月15日に国際天文学連合は系外惑星の最初の固有名の発表を行った。

The global video streaming market is expected to be worth $184.27 billion by 2027. Technological advancements, including the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance video quality, are set to increase the demand for online video content in upcoming years. Additionally, the fact that publishers use social media platforms to increase the reach of their content is influencing the market growth.
The rise of the industry is happening at the time when internet users and brands are turning towards virtual events, remote work, and distance learning. In this environment, video plays a leading role.
As the market is expanding, there is one issue on everyone’s mind: cybersecurity threats. Most industries are riddled with hacking, piracy, and digital attacks, and the online video market is no exception.
Ad fraud is affecting the online advertising industry, costing publishers millions of dollars. Find out more about it here.
However, these threats can be minimized with the help of video security solutions. AES video encryption, in particular, is valuable for brands that want to protect their content on the internet.
But what is AES video encryption? We will discuss this, how it works, and more in our article!
Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is a symmetric block cipher used for encrypting and decrypting sensitive data throughout the world. This algorithm type has proven to be valuable for various industries, including online video streaming.
Whenever publishers deliver audio and video media across the internet they utilize transfer protocols such as HTTP, FTP, or SFTP. To ensure secure streaming, some of them rely on AES video encryption. This protects data and guarantees that only intended parties will be able to watch and access video content.
When AES encrypts a video, it produces a special key. Authorized video players decode this key in browsers where the stream is delivered with the help of secure transfer protocols. These players rely on symmetric-key algorithms to decrypt ciphertext and provide meaningful content.
The entire process is completely transparent. Internet users need to gain access to the video, either by logging in to their accounts or accessing a website. After this AES video encryption comes into play, enabling those users to securely watch online video content.
But why was AES developed in the first place?
As you know, video encryption is the process that hides videos from unintended audiences. AES is one way to achieve this. But how did AES come to be?
Previously, the go-to encryption method was Data Encryption Standard (DES), developed by IBM. Even the US government used it to secure sensitive information. DES was considered to be uncrackable for years, but technological advancements proved that it was possible to break the 56-bit encryption algorithm.
In 1997, the DESCHALL Project publicly broke a message encrypted with DES. This meant that a successor to DES was greatly needed.
